entries.note: The main assertion, that this is bad news, is an evaluative judgment. Its consistency with his earlier warning is separately verifiable.

entries.test: Provider revenue disclosures and enterprise spending reports could establish whether tokenmaxxing generated substantial short-term revenue for Anthropic and OpenAI.
entries.note: The causal revenue claim is checkable; the sustainability reservation reports his assessment rather than making a firm forecast.
He reproduces and endorses his own earlier value judgment.

entries.test: Public customer accounts of accidentally consuming half a billion tokens in a month would show whether customers accept that consumption comfortably or object to it.
entries.note: The plain reading predicts customer rejection of accidental consumption at this scale. No deadline is specified.

entries.test: Public provider financial results, pricing changes, and enterprise usage reports could establish whether retreat from tokenmaxxing reduces revenue or drives lower prices and worsens profitability.
entries.note: The quoted enterprise trend is attributed to Ansari, but Marcus supplies and endorses the causal inference.

entries.test: Dated public reports and Marcus's public references to them could establish whether reports of enterprise token spending without significant ROI were becoming more frequent.
entries.note: This asserts an observable reporting trend without independently endorsing every allegation in the embedded posts.
“Could get worse” asserts a possibility under the stated condition, not a firm outcome.

entries.test: Public announcements and government financial records would establish whether bailouts occur in response to the AI downturn he describes.
entries.note: “Brace for” conveys an expectation of bailouts in this context. He supplies no deadline.
